text:
OpenAI released o3 and o4-mini on April 16, 2025 [Source: ev-1]. The launch signaled a direction for frontier reasoning models characterized by native integration of vision and tool use (web search, code interpreter) directly into the model architecture rather than bolting them on [Source: ev-1]. It also established an API-first availability strategy where developers had access from day one, with o3 initially excluded from the ChatGPT app while o4-mini was included [Source: ev-1].

The release highlighted OpenAI's adoption of "budget forcing," which uses task-adaptive dynamic compute to allow harder questions to think longer within a fixed maximum thought budget [Source: ev-1]. Additionally, it introduced OpenAI’s first private chain-of-thought policy, keeping reasoning tokens hidden from API callers as announced in the system card [Source: ev-1]. Strategically, with GPT-5 not yet shipping, OpenAI used this launch to defend its position against DeepSeek R1 and Anthropic by reframing frontier capability as tool-using reasoning available at commodity prices, exemplified by o3 pricing at $10 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens, and o4-mini at $1.10 per million input tokens and 4.40 dollars per million output tokens [Source: ev-1]. The models also demonstrated significant performance gains, with o3 setting a record on ARC-AGI-1 at high compute of about 87.5%, reaching or exceeding the ~85% human baseline for the first time [Source: ev-1].
